newsitem.title: UK: Five London stations closed in security alert.
newsitem.headline: Five London stations closed in security alert.

text.p: British police closed five London railway stations on Monday after receiving what they called "threatening phone calls".
A police spokeswoman said roads were being closed and all five stations were being evacuated but it was too early to say whether any bombs or other devices had been found.
Parts of Heathrow airport west of London were also evacuated, police said.
"We have had a number of threatening phone calls. We are treating them with caution," the spokeswoman told Reuters.
She said mainline stations at King's Cross, Charing Cross, Paddington and St Pancras were being evacuated as was the underground station at Baker Street.

The early morning closures at the start of the Monday rush hour caused chaos on the capital's transport system and followed a series of similar security alerts in north-west England last week blamed on IRA guerrillas.
The Irish Republican Army, which is seeking an end to British rule in Northern Ireland, has stepped up its campaign to coincide with the runup to British national elections on May 1.
